subject: URGENT: Acme Robotics - sudden p99 spike and 500s (KV cache thrash)
messages:

Cc: Acme Ops <ops@acmerobotics.com>

Subject: Re: Production errors - urgent

Camila —

We started seeing a big regression in our inference routes this morning. p99 latency jumped from ~220ms to >1.2s and we started getting intermittent 500s around 08:40 PDT. Throughput to your endpoint dropped by ~30%. We attached a screenshot and a short list of request IDs. Can you take a look? This is impacting our scheduling microservice which uses your reranking endpoints.

We only rolled a small prompt change yesterday and nothing on our side changed in routing. Please escalate — we need an ETA.

Thanks,

Tom —

Thanks for the heads up and the traces. I'm pulling in engineering now. First pass: can you confirm whether these request IDs include any long-context requests (>2k tokens) or streaming calls? Also whether you were pinned to model:v2.4 or using auto model routing?

Marissa & Sean — can you triage KV/caching and batching metrics for Acme's routes (acme-rerank-prod) from 08:00–09:30 PDT and surface any KV eviction spikes, hot-lane metrics, or batch-lane starvation? Share earliest screenshots.

I'll keep Tom updated.

Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors - urgent

Camila / Sean —

Quick triage summary (08:00–09:30 PDT):
- Observed sudden spike in KV cache evictions for shard group acme-* starting at 08:37. Eviction rate rose ~8x vs baseline.
- HOT_PARTITION ratio increased on 2 of 6 hotlanes (hot-lane-3 & hot-lane-5).
- Batch lane logs show frequent micro-burst batching where batch size collapsed to 1 for many requests -> reduces throughput and increases per-token cost.
- A correlated increase in model fallback rate: 12% of requests were auto-falling back to model:v2.2 (lower perf variant) due to 503s from primary nodes.

I pulled kv-metrics-20270430.csv and request-traces-logs-reqids.txt (attached). Preliminary hypothesis: aggressive short TTL + mismatched prefix hashing caused churn in per-shard caches, combined with a recent config tweak that widened batching windows for lower latency; that widened window under this workload allowed HOL (head-of-line) blocking when large KV misses forced long-tail model fetches.

Mitigation steps I suggest immediately:
1) Reduce KV eviction pressure by increasing per-shard cache budget for acme-* by 20% (runtime config).
2) Temporarily lower batching window to previous conservative value (reduces HOL exposure).
3) Disable auto model fallback policy for acme-rerank-prod while we stabilize to avoid loading slower model variants and confusing the capacity planner.

I can push (1) & (2) as a config hotfix with a canary in 2 nodes in the next 15 minutes if agreed.

-Marissa
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmerobotics.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors - urgent

Tom / Team —

Thanks, Marissa — that aligns with traces. Tom: we saw a traffic pattern shift around 08:35 where tens of thousands of short requests with high key variance hit the reranker; that flush + short KV TTL (recently changed to 4s to optimize freshness) led to constant cold misses. Each cold miss triggers KV recompute that holds the batch lane while the request waits on KV IO -> head-of-line blocking for concurrent small requests.

Action plan I executed at 10:15 PDT (now):
- Pushed per-shard cache budget +25% for acme-* (canary on 2 nodes -> rolled to 6 nodes).
- Reverted KV TTL from 4s -> 12s for acme routes (should reduce miss rate).
- Reverted batching window to 6ms (from 12ms).
- Disabled auto-fallback to v2.2 for acme-rerank-prod.

Early telemetry (10:21–10:30): p99 dropped from 1.2s -> ~310ms; 500s frequency down by ~85%. Throughput trending back up. We're monitoring for 30min before rolling config cluster-wide.

I'll loop back with a formal RCA and permanent config recommendations.

-Sean
Director, Production Engineering

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmerobotics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors - urgent

Tom —

Short answers and next steps:
- Quick RCA (summary): The immediate cause was KV cache churn triggered by a recent reduction in TTL combined with a burst of high-variance short requests. That churn caused frequent cold misses that triggered slow KV recomputations. Those recomputations blocked batch lanes, producing head-of-line blocking and a cascade of 503s and auto-fallbacks.
- Why we disabled fallback: fallback to v2.2 increases request load across model variants and confused the capacity planner while the cache churn persisted. In practice it masked the cache problem by shifting load unpredictably; disabling fallback is temporary until we stabilize cache hit rate and adjust autoscaler thresholds. We'll re-enable once we have stable metrics.

Permanent mitigations we will implement in the next sprint:
1) Add workload-aware TTL heuristics: route-specific TTL bounds that adapt to request-size distribution.
2) Introduce a short-circuit for cold KV misses that prevents head-of-line blocking (serve partial result + async recompute).
3) Improve batch-lane isolation: reserve small fast lanes for short low-latency requests to avoid HOL impact if a batch member triggers long KV IO.
4) Update our runbook and add an automated rollback knob for TTL/batching changes.

Camila — I'll draft the customer-facing incident note and a slide for execs. Marissa/Sean: please attach the telemetry snapshots and exact config diffs to the Jira INF-8721 by EOD. Tom: we'll schedule the technical review for next Tue; I will send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Serving Runtime
